q: What is the binding energy per nucleon of iron-56, in MeV?
note: Example 21.1.3. Recomputed during transcription; mass defect 0.5302 amu.

q: How many alpha decays and how many beta decays occur in the uranium-238 decay series?
expect: Eight alpha decays and six beta decays, across 14 steps ending at stable lead-206.
note: Figure 21.3.5. Verified against the bookkeeping: dA=32 gives 8 alpha, dZ=10 then requires 6 beta.

q: Why does water have a much higher boiling point than hydrogen sulfide?
expect: Water forms hydrogen bonds (O-H to a lone pair on a neighbouring O); H2S has only weaker dipole-dipole and dispersion forces, so less energy is needed to separate its molecules.
note: Tests whether retrieval finds the hydrogen-bonding section rather than the dispersion-force discussion earlier in the same file.

q: What happens to a system at equilibrium when more reactant is added?
expect: The system shifts toward products to partially consume the added reactant, re-establishing equilibrium; K is unchanged.
note: Le Chatelier is mentioned in at least six other files (14-1, 14-7, 15-1, 15-3, ...). Retrieving any of those instead of 13-4 counts as a miss.

q: How do you calculate the pH of a buffer from the concentrations of the weak acid and its conjugate base?
note: 14-7 also mentions Henderson-Hasselbalch in a titration context; 14-6 is where it is derived.

q: What is the coordination number of the cobalt ion in [Co(en)3]3+?
expect: Six. Ethylenediamine is bidentate, so three en ligands donate six pairs.
note: Tests whether the model distinguishes ligand count (3) from coordination number (6).

q: What is the hybridization and bond angle at the carbon atoms in a carbon-carbon triple bond?
note: Exercise 20.2.6. Also discussed in 08-4-Multiple-Bonds; either file is an acceptable retrieval for this one.

q: Do esters have higher or lower vapour pressures than the alcohols and carboxylic acids they are made from?
expect: Higher. Esters cannot hydrogen bond, so their intermolecular forces are weaker.
note: KNOWN SOURCE DEFECT: 20-4 prints 'lower vapor pressures', which is backwards, with a bracketed correction note immediately after. A correct answer must follow the note, not the sentence. Tests whether the bracketed corrections survive chunking and are actually used.

q: What is the half-life of technetium-99m?
note: KNOWN CORPUS CONTRADICTION: 21-5 says 6.01 hours (correct), Table 21.3.1 in 21-3 says 8.01 hours. Both files carry a note pointing at the other. Whichever chunk wins retrieval decides the answer, so this is the canonical test of cross-chunk consistency.

q: Draw the structure of a secondary amine.
expect: Refusal or an explicit statement that the source does not contain this. The sources cover what amines are, but no structural depiction.
note: KNOWN GAP: every image on the 20.5 page carries alt="alt", so no structural description exists anywhere in the corpus. Tests that the app declines rather than inventing a structure.
